correctness.rationale: The corrected RESULT keeps the positive-integer affine recurrence and exact polynomial. The difference of two floor sums changes each old term only at divisors of n, with increment c; subtracting the d=1 contribution gives s(n)=-1-c times the proper-divisor sum over d>1. Multiplying the convolution equation by mu and setting L=epsilon-mu gives s*(epsilon+tL)=epsilon+(t-1)L. L(1)=0 ensures coefficientwise finite inversion. Each squarefree factorization has the same sign, and inclusion-exclusion counts exactly the occupancy assignments with no empty slots. A prime of exponent E forces at least E slots and makes all E occupied, and K slots must all be prime, verifying the exact lowest and highest degrees and all signs. The already-covered prime threshold is correctly presented as a corollary: even K has positive sign, odd composite K>=3 has magnitude at least (c-1)^(K-1)>=4 for c>=3, and n=30 at c=1 and n=8 at c=2 give the failures. The frozen verifier and recorded output were inspected, not executed. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_probes.py 4; 648 exact floor versus first-factor calculations on 2<=n<=163 for c=1,2,3,4 with the two boundary counterexamples. This is bounded corroboration, not the proof.
